sources.citation: Pelkey, Jamin R. 2011. A Phula Comparative Lexicon: Phola, Phuza, Muji, Phowa, Azha. SIL Language and Culture Documentation and Description 18. Dallas: SIL International. 144 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: SILENT. Its Phowa sketch (sec. 3.4, pp. 9-10) is of Hlepho-FZK, a sister language; Ani Phowa-DHN (Daheineng, Xibeile Twp, Mengzi) appears only in the datapoint list (p. 3), the Phowa meso-clade section (pp. 16-17, tone-class reflexes) and lexicon footnotes. 'stress'/'accent' occur 0 times in the book.

sources.citation: Pelkey, Jamin R. 2005. Puzzling over Phula: Toward the synthesis and statement of a sub-branch. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 28(2): 43-78. doi 10.32655/ltba.28.2.02. Sec. 6.1 'Ani Phowa: a newly described Phula variety', pp. 58-60 (data 'adapted from Pelkey (2004)').
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: SILENT. The Ani Phowa sketch gives 42 consonant initials, 11 vowel finals, 'five tonal contrasts: high /55/, mid /33/, low /22/, low-rising /13/, and low-falling /21/' and a tense-lax phonation contrast; the words stress/accent/prominence/intonation/rhythm never occur in a technical sense in the whole article (stress(ed) only pp. 48, 50 non-technically).

sources.citation: Pelkey, Jamin R. 2004. Phowa verbal semantics. MA thesis, Payap University, Chiang Mai. xxi+189 pp. (preliminary phonology sketch of Ani Phowa-DHN, grammar sketch, 927-item wordlist, interlinearized narrative).
